questions.stemHtml: Which of the following joints is not formed by the structure shown in the picture?
questions.solutionHtml:
Synchondrosis
  • A synchondrosis (or primary cartilaginous joint) is a type of cartilaginous joint where hyaline cartilage completely joins together two bones.
  • Synchondroses are different from symphyses (secondary cartilaginous joints), which are formed of fibrocartilage, and from synostosis (ossified junctions), which is the fusion of two or more bones. Synchondroses are immovable joints and are thus referred to as synarthroses.

Parts of vertebrae and articulation

questions.stemHtml: The marked part in the first image has a direct connection with which of the following parts marked in the second image?
questions.solutionHtml:
2
  • The arrow marked structure in the first image is the middle cerebellar peduncle.
  • The marked part in the first image has a direct connection with the red nucleus.
  • Red nucleus controls the pattern of movement and postural reflexes.
  • Its main connection is cerebellum, reticular formation, spinal cord sensori motor cortex.

First Image

  1. Pons
  2. Middle cerebellar peduncle
  3. White matter of cerebellum
  4. Cortex or gray matter of cerebellum

Second image is transverse section of midbrain

The midbrain consists of four main parts:

  • Tectum(1)
  • Red nucleus(2)
  • Substantia nigra (3)
  • Crus cerebri (4)

The most prominent structure in the tegmentum is the red nucleus but the tegmentum also contains ascending tracts.





Human Anatomy by BD Chourasia’s, 8th Edition, Volume 4, Page No. 112.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not seen in the floor of the inferior horn of the lateral ventricle?
questions.solutionHtml:
Tail of caudate nucleus
  • Tail of the caudate nucleus forms the medial part of the roof of the inferior horn of the lateral ventricle.

questions.stem: Spinal sensory nucleus of the trigeminal has 2nd order neurons to carry which sensation?
questions.solutionHtml:
Pain

questions.stemHtml: The nerve marked in the picture has its root value from?

options.label: D
options.text: Dorsal root ganglia of T1 and T2

questions.solutionHtml:
Ventral horn of C4
  • A marked structure is anterior to hilum lung, and the marked structure is phrenic nerve.
  • The phrenic nerve is formed from the ventral roots of C3–C5; its primary component arises from the C4 anterior primary ramus.

questions.stem: Professor underwent a left parotidectomy. Post surgery she complaints of left lower lip paralysis. Which structure is involved?
questions.solutionHtml:
Facial nerve cervical branch
  • Few literature suggests that the cervical branch of the facial nerve is responsible for innervating the inferior labial depressor, elucidating the relatively elevated occurrence of partial lower lip palsy .
  • The functionality of this muscle holds significance in smile aesthetics, speech, and articulation.


Human Anatomy by BD Chourasia’s, 8th Edition, Volume 3, Page No. 80-83.

questions.stemHtml: The area marked by the arrow is supplied by which of the following arteries?
questions.solutionHtml:
Anterior inter ventricular artery
  • The “A” marked structure is interventricular septum.
  • The anterior interventricular branch of the left coronary artery supplies the adjacent portions of right and left ventricle.
  • It also supplies the anterior two thirds of the interventricular septum as well as the atrioventricular bundle.


Human Anatomy by BD Chourasia’s, 8th Edition, Volume 1, Page No. 299-300.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true with respect to anatomy of the breast?

options.label: A
options.text: Superior medial quadrant contains more glandular tissue

options.label: B
options.text: Ligament of cooper found only in upper quadrant

options.label: C
options.text: Tail of spence extends across anterior axillary fold

questions.answerText: Tail of spence extends across anterior axillary fold
questions.solutionHtml:
Tail of spence extends across anterior axillary fold
  • “The axillary tail of Spence” refers to a contiguous extension of adipose angling superolaterally from the primary breast into the axilla.
